The proposed derivation conflates the spectral radius with the revival condition and overlooks the detailed phase relationships required for fractional revival between antipodal vertices. The eigenvalue structure of \(X=\text{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{2p},\mathbb{Z}_{2p}^{\times})\) is more intricate (it includes three distinct eigenvalues \(p-1,\;-(p-1)\) and \(-1\) with different multiplicities), and the fractional‑revival condition requires that the phases \(e^{-i\lambda_j t}\) align in a very specific way for all eigenvalues. Simply setting \(e^{-i(p-1)t}=1\) (which yields \(t=2\pi/(p-1)\)) does not satisfy these constraints, as can be seen by evaluating the transition amplitudes for small primes (e.g. \(p=3,5\)). Hence the closed‑form expression \(\displaystyle t^{*}= \frac{2\pi}{p-1}\) is not correct.

**Verdict:** REJECT (the final answer is not correct)
